steps.text: Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together in a mixing bowl. Cut in shortening with a knife or pastry blender until mixture resembles fine crumbs. Stir milk into flour mixture until moistened. Dough will be pretty lumpy, but be sure to not over mix it!

Drop dough by large spoonfuls onto any simmering stew. The dumplings should rest on top of vegetables and meat; it's okay if they stick out of the top a bit. Cook uncovered for 10 minutes; cover and cook another 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom's Simple Dumplings
raw_recipe.description: This easy recipe makes delicious dumpling dough to be dropped on top of chicken stew or soup as it simmers for a hearty and comforting bowl of food.
raw_recipe.name: Mom's Simple Dumplings

review.reviewBody: I was looking for a recipe that would make drop dumplings as easily as Bisquick but without the Bisquick's fake ingredients. This is it! Perfectly soft and puffy. Only change I made was to use butter rather than shortening.

We like dumplings in beef stew and I've never been able to make really good ones. Until yesterday. I made them too large really but it didn't matter. They were perfect, light and tender all the way through. My only change was to add coarsely ground pepper. I'll halve the size next time but I'll use this recipe.

Good old fashioned bread dumplings! Simple and perfect for stew. I added a tablespoon of dried parsley flakes for color but that's it. You can add other herbs but why ... the simplicity of this dumpling compliments and doesn't compete with the stew's gravy. After plopping mine on top of the stew I covered with a lid and turned heat to the lowest setting for 10 minutes and then turned off the heat and left them rest while still covered for another 10 minutes. They puffed up nice and had a wholesome goodness to them.
Perfect! The exact recipe I was looking for. I added some herbs and spices before mixing in the milk and they were fabulous in stew. Thanks for sharing :)

I sauteed carrots, celery, onions, garlic and a bay leaf together and then added some diced chicken breast. Thickened with cornstarch added salt and pepper to taste and then made these dumplings. They were great. They did not turn out as pictured but maybe my broth was more bubbly. Still they were chewy on the outside and bread like in the middle which is exactly how I want my dumplings. I did use butter instead of shortening. Thank you for the great recipe I will use over and over.
Followed the recipe. Very good. Was able to reheat the dumplings by very carefully removing them from cold soup, heating soup to a slow simmer and dropping dumplings back on top for about 10 minutes.

We all loved these! I used butter instead of shortening. I baked the leftovers just like you would biscuits and my family devoured them. I'm looking into using this recipe as a dry mix so we can have dumplings/biscuits at the drop of a hat.

Very fast, easy, and delicious; a must-have for winter stews and soups! The only thing I changed was to use butter instead of shortening, and cut back the salt to 1/2 tsp since the butter I used was salted. My husband told me he would love it if I served these with every soup or stew we eat.

The dumplings turned out great. The dumplings didn’t thicken up as much as I would have liked. My next batch I will use 2 cups of flour. 1 1/2 cups for the dumplings, with the remaining 1/2 cup to be mixed with a little butter and added in as a thickening agent. They should be great!
Better than Bisquick, just as easy to make, and tastes so much better. I used the butter option rather than shortening. This recipe is definitely a keeper.
Easy and fast. Made mine to go with a rustic lamb stew using red fife flour for them. Great taste and texture. Rose well. Used butter and seasoned with mixed herbs
I just made this and cooked uncovered for 6min then covered for 14min and turned out so darn good. Thank you for the recipe.
Used heavy cream and water instead of milk just to use up the cream
This recipe is easy to make and they turn out perfectly every time. I added just a little poultry seasoning.
Delicious I use this dumpljng recipe in all my homeade soups and chilli love it and everyone in my family and all my friends love them too soft and goes wj derfully with soups of all kinds

An old recipe that I was makng 60 years ago. I did add an egg. My sons all 5 of them begged for chicken and especially the dumplings. So tasty and easy. Depending on what I was making the dumplings on determined what I threw on them. Parsley, garlic, italian seasoning, etc.

I've been making something very close to this recipe for over 40 years. My grandmother taught me when I was just 10 (I'm 53 now). This recipe is so easy and makes some delicious dumplings. I make them for soups, stews, and anything with sauerkraut. You won't go wrong with this recipe!
They turned out great and so easy.

Simple recipe that can't fail. I have made these for years. If you bake them in the oven then they are biscuits. I have made them using oil, lard, shortening or butter and they always turn out. I steamed them for the full 20 minutes with the lid on as opposed to half time with the lid off. I also sprinkle them with a little dried parsely or oregano.
Everyone loved it ...no left overs
